info.title: Aphel API
info.description:
REST API of Aphel. Everything the interface does goes through here: records of every installed plugin, custom fields, imports and configuration.

## Authentication

Create a token in **Settings → API tokens**, choosing the scopes (`people:read`, `deals:write`…) and the expiration. The token is shown only once; send it on every request:

```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer aphel_3f9a1c2b_…" https://your-aphel.example.com/api/v1/people
```

The token acts on behalf of whoever created it and can never do more than that person can **at the time of the request**: the effective permission is the intersection of the scopes with that person's current permissions. A revoked or expired token, or one belonging to a deactivated user, responds `401 invalid_api_token`; insufficient scope, `403 insufficient_scope`. Session and account routes (`/auth/*`, `/api-tokens`) only accept the browser session.

## Limits

Each token has a sliding window (default: 600 requests per minute). Every response carries `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining` and `X-RateLimit-Reset` (seconds). When exceeded, `429 rate_limited` with `Retry-After`.

## Responses and pagination

- Item: `{ "data": { ... } }`.
- List: `{ "data": [ ... ], "meta": { "total": 120, "page": 1, "per_page": 25 } }`, with `?page=` (≥ 1) and `?per_page=` (1–100).
- Cursor lists (timeline): `{ "data": [ ... ], "meta": { "next_cursor": "..." } }`.
- Dates in ISO-8601 UTC (`2026-10-20T13:45:00Z`), money as a decimal string with currency (`"amount": "15000.00", "currency": "BRL"`), custom fields in `custom_fields`.

## Filters, sorting and relationships

```bash
# simple form: conditions combined with "and"
curl -G -H "Authorization: Bearer $APHEL_TOKEN" "$APHEL_URL/api/v1/deals" \
  --data-urlencode "filter[status][eq]=open" \
  --data-urlencode "filter[amount][gte]=1000" \
  --data-urlencode "sort=-amount,title"

# full form: the filter tree as JSON
curl -G -H "Authorization: Bearer $APHEL_TOKEN" "$APHEL_URL/api/v1/people" \
  --data-urlencode 'filter={"op":"or","conditions":[{"field":"email","operator":"contains","value":"@acme"},{"field":"city","operator":"eq","value":"Recife"}]}'
```

`include=company,owner` embeds allowed relationships (listed on each route).

## Safe writes

- `PATCH` is partial; send `If-Match: <updated_at>` to avoid overwriting someone else's change (`409 version_conflict`).
- Send `Idempotency-Key: <uuid>` on `POST` so you can repeat the request without duplicating the record: the same key with the same body returns the original response (`Idempotent-Replayed: true`).

## Errors

Always `{ "error": { "code", "message", "details" } }`. Decide based on the `code`, which is stable; `details.fields` points to invalid fields in `422 validation_error`.

## Complete example

```bash
export APHEL_URL=https://your-aphel.example.com APHEL_TOKEN=aphel_…
company=$(curl -s -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $APHEL_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name":"Acme Ltda","custom_fields":{}}' "$APHEL_URL/api/v1/organizations" | jq -r .data.id)
contact=$(curl -s -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $APHEL_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{\"first_name\":\"Bruna\",\"company_id\":\"$company\",\"custom_fields\":{}}" "$APHEL_URL/api/v1/people" | jq -r .data.id)
curl -s -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $APHEL_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{\"title\":\"Acme onboarding\",\"amount\":\"15000.00\",\"currency\":\"BRL\",\"company_id\":\"$company\",\"contact_id\":\"$contact\",\"custom_fields\":{}}" \
  "$APHEL_URL/api/v1/deals"
```

Compatibility: contract-breaking changes only ship in `/api/v2` (policy in the repository, `docs/api/versioning.md`).

post.description: Aggregates records of a type under the read scope of the caller (`own`/`team`/`organization`) and the field permissions of the role, in the time zone of the organization. `group_by` (up to 3) accepts system and custom fields (select, multi-select and user included), `tags`, `owner_team` (team of the owner; an owner in two teams counts in both) and fields of a single related record such as `company.industry` on deals; date fields take a `granularity` (`day`, `week` starting on Monday, `month`, `quarter`, `year`, default `day`) and their bucket key is the first day of the bucket (`YYYY-MM-DD`). `metrics` (up to 10, default `[{"fn":"count"}]`): `count` (distinct records, or records with a value when `field` is given) and `sum`/`avg`/`min`/`max` over number or currency fields of the type itself; the key of a metric is `fn` or `fn:field`. A duration metric takes two date or date and time fields of the type itself, `field` (start) and `to` (end), and a `unit` (`days`, the default, or `hours`): it applies `fn` (`count`/`sum`/`avg`/`min`/`max`) to the time between both dates of each record (fractional, records missing either date are skipped), such as `{"fn":"avg","field":"created_at","to":"closed_at"}` for the average days to close; its key is `fn:field..to:unit`. `filter` is the same AST of the listings and also accepts conditions on related records (`company.industry`, `deals.status` on organization_profile), each evaluated as "there is a related record visible to the caller that matches" so totals are never duplicated, and `owner_team` with `in`/`not_in`/`is_empty`/`is_not_empty`. `period` limits a date field to a preset (`today`, `yesterday`, `last_7_days`, `last_30_days`, `week`, `last_week`, `month`, `last_month`, `quarter`, `last_quarter`, `year`, `last_year`) or a `custom` range (`from`/`to`, at most 731 days); with `compare_to_previous` every row and the totals also carry `previous`, computed over the period right before (whole months shift by months, any other range by its length) and matched bucket by bucket when grouping by the period field. Rows grouped only by the period field fill empty buckets with zero. `sort` takes group fields or metric keys (default: groups ascending, select options in the order of their position, empty values last); `limit` defaults to 500 (max 1000) and `truncated` tells when more groups exist. Values are decimal strings; sums ignore the currency of each record.

post.description: Creates an approval policy (`approval_policy.created`). The policy applies to records of `record_type` at a `moment`: `stage_change` (before a record with stages moves to the stage `target_id`), `quote_send` (before a quote is sent) or `on_demand` (when someone or an automation asks for it). The condition is `always`, a `filter` validated against the fields of the type (same format as views) or a boolean `formula`; it is evaluated over the stored record with every field visible. Steps run in order (1 to 10): approvers are a `user`, the members of a `role` or the managers of the teams of the record owner (`owner_team_manager`), with rule `any` (one approval closes the step) or `all`. When a step resolves nobody besides the requester, the members with `approvals.manage` approve it; the requester never approves their own request, and when nobody is eligible the request is refused with 409 `approval_no_approver` instead of staying pending forever. While a request is pending, `locked_fields` (empty = whole record) cannot be changed (409 `approval_pending`). Needs `approvals.manage`.

post.description: Asks for the approvals a record needs at a moment (`on_demand`, `stage_change` with `target_id` = stage, `quote_send`), usually after a 409 `approval_required`. For every active policy of the type and moment whose condition matches the record, opens a request (`approval.requested`, approvers of the first step notified) unless one is already pending or approved and not yet used. `policy_key` restricts the submission to one policy. `outcome` is `not_required` (no policy applies), `pending` or `approved` (every applicable policy already approved: retry the change). Needs edit access to the record.

post.description: Approves the current step as one of its approvers. With rule `any` the step closes; with `all` it closes when every approver approved (`approval.decision_recorded` meanwhile). A closed step opens the next one (`approval.step_advanced`, new approvers notified); the last one approves the request (`approval.approved`, requester notified). The approved request is used by the next matching change of the record.

200.description: Merges `duplicate_id` into `primary_id` in one transaction. `fields` chooses, per field key (system or custom), which record's value stays (`primary` or `duplicate`); omitted fields keep the primary value unless it is empty. Fields hidden from the user cannot be chosen: their values stay on the primary and are only filled from the duplicate when empty (redacted in the audit). Activities, notes, attachments, tags, relationships, record references, deals and company links (people), people and deals (organizations) or rows of other types that point to it (other types) move to the primary; the duplicate goes to the trash and its id redirects to the primary. The duplicate keeps its own custom values in the trash (restoring it brings them back), while the moved links stay with the primary. Both writes go through the record pipeline: the primary update runs validation rules, approvals and the other `RecordValidating` hooks and publishes `<type>.updated` (when something changed), the duplicate runs `RecordDeleting`/`RecordDeleted` and publishes `<type>.deleted`; `<type>.merged` is published as well

The currency, contact and company come from the deal; the owner defaults to the caller; `valid_until` and `terms` default to the quote settings; the price list defaults to the best active list for the currency and company. `from_line_items: true` copies the deal items; otherwise send `items`. post.description: Creates a scoring model (`scoring_model.created`) for a record type (`contact`, `company`, `deal` or a custom object) and queues a full recalculation. The first model of a record type becomes its primary model, exposed as the read-only `score` field. Needs `scoring.manage`.

A term that looks like a phone number (only digits, spaces and `+()-./`, 6 to 15 digits) is searched by its digits, so `11 99999-8888`, `999998888` and `+55 11 99999-8888` all find `+5511999998888`. Indexed fields: searchable system fields and custom fields flagged searchable of the text, long text, e-mail, phone and URL types; sensitive fields are never indexed. Each type is searched only when the caller has its read permission, with the own/team/organization scope of that permission, the pipeline restriction of deals, soft delete, archive and merges applied by revalidating the candidates through the record query engine; fields hidden from the role are neither matched nor used for `title`/`subtitle`. `types` (comma separated) limits and orders the groups (unknown types answer 422); without it groups come by best relevance. `limit` is per type (default 5, max 20) and items are ordered by relevance (`score`). `total` counts the visible matches among the first 100 candidates of the type. Types without matches are omitted. The index is updated by the `search.index` consumer and rebuilt with `aphel search reindex`.

Needs `sequences.manage`.

post.description: Installs or upgrades a plugin from an `.aphelplugin` package sent as the multipart field `package` (permission `system.manage`). The package is a zip with `plugin.toml`, an optional `backend.wasm` built with aphel-plugin-sdk and an optional `web/` bundle. Declared entities become custom objects managed by the plugin, declared fields become managed custom fields, declared permissions enter the role catalog, and hooks, events, schedules and routes start working without restarting Aphel. The plugin acts with what it `requires` intersected with the permissions of whoever installs it, so the installer gives consent: call first with `dry_run=true` to get what the package asks for (status 200, nothing is installed). Integrated frontend code runs with the browser session, independently of backend capabilities; packages with web code require acknowledge_web_version=<manifest version> on each install or upgrade, including upgrades kept disabled. Dry runs need no admission. Publishes `plugin.installed`.

post.description: Installs or upgrades a plugin pack: an `.aphelpack` zip with `pack.toml` and the `.aphelplugin` packages it lists, sent as the multipart field `package` (permission `system.manage`). The plugins are installed in dependency order (a plugin that calls an operation or listens to an event of another plugin of the pack comes after it). Every plugin is validated before anything is installed; call first with `dry_run=true` to get each plugin's consent, action (`install`, `upgrade`, `unchanged`), error and the pack settings that will apply. Plugins whose package did not change are skipped. Pack settings fill only the settings that have no value yet. `acknowledge_web_version=<pack version>` admits the integrated frontend code of every plugin of the pack. If a plugin fails while installing, the following ones are skipped and the response is 207; sending the pack again continues from there. `requires_aphel` and `requires_modules` are checked first (`plugin_pack_aphel_incompatible`, `plugin_pack_module_unavailable`); required modules that are disabled are enabled before the plugins (the module that administers objects counts as required when a plugin declares entities). After the plugins, the `[[provision]]` resources are created in dependency order and reported in `provisions` (`created`, `updated`, `kept`, `user_changed`, `removed`, `failed`, `skipped`); a failed resource makes the response 207 and is retried on the next install. Publishes `plugin.pack_installed`.
